NKJV.1: Again David gathered all the choice men of Israel, thirty thousand.
NKJV.2: And David arose and went with all the people who were with him from Baale Judah to bring up from there the ark of God, whose name is called by the Name, the LORD of Hosts, who dwells between the cherubim.
NKJV.3: So they set the ark of God on a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new cart.
NKJV.4: And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill, accompanying the ark of God; and Ahio went before the ark.
NKJV.5: Then David and all the house of Israel played music before the LORD on all kinds of instruments of fir wood, on harps, on stringed instruments, on tambourines, on sistrums, and on cymbals.
NKJV.6: And when they came to Nachon’s threshing floor, Uzzah put out his hand to the ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled.
NKJV.7: Then the anger of the LORD was aroused against Uzzah, and God struck him there for his error; and he died there by the ark of God.
NKJV.8: And David became angry because of the LORD’s outbreak against Uzzah; and he called the name of the place Perez Uzzah to this day.
NKJV.9: David was afraid of the LORD that day; and he said, “How can the ark of the LORD come to me?”
NKJV.10: So David would not move the ark of the LORD with him into the City of David; but David took it aside into the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.
NKJV.11: The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite three months. And the LORD blessed Obed-Edom and all his household.
NKJV.12: Now it was told King David, saying, “The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-Edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God.” So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom to the City of David with gladness.
NKJV.13: And so it was, when those bearing the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, that he sacrificed oxen and fatted sheep.
NKJV.14: Then David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was wearing a linen ephod.
NKJV.15: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and with the sound of the trumpet.
NKJV.16: Now as the ark of the LORD came into the City of David, Michal, Saul’s daughter, looked through a window and saw King David leaping and whirling before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart.
NKJV.17: So they brought the ark of the LORD, and set it in its place in the midst of the tabernacle that David had erected for it. Then David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
NKJV.18: And when David had finished offering burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.
NKJV.19: Then he distributed among all the people, among the whole multitude of Israel, both the women and the men, to everyone a loaf of bread, a piece of meat, and a cake of raisins. So all the people departed, everyone to his house.
NKJV.20: Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, “How glorious was the king of Israel today, uncovering himself today in the eyes of the maids of his servants, as one of the base fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!”
NKJV.21: So David said to Michal, “It was before the LORD, who chose me instead of your father and all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel. Therefore I will play music before the LORD.
NKJV.22: And I will be even more undignified than this, and will be humble in my own sight. But as for the maidservants of whom you have spoken, by them I will be held in honor.”
NKJV.23: Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no children to the day of her death.

ESV.1: David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.
ESV.2: And David arose and went with all the people who were with him from Baale-judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the name of the LORD of hosts who sits enthroned on the cherubim.
ESV.3: And they carried the ark of God on a new cart and brought it out of the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill. And Uzzah and Ahio,  the sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart,
ESV.4: with the ark of God,  and Ahio went before the ark.
ESV.5: And David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD, with songs  and lyres and harps and tambourines and castanets and cymbals.
ESV.6: And when they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah put out his hand to the ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled.
ESV.7: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah, and God struck him down there because of his error, and he died there beside the ark of God.
ESV.8: And David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah. And that place is called Perez-uzzah  to this day.
ESV.9: And David was afraid of the LORD that day, and he said, “How can the ark of the LORD come to me?”
ESV.10: So David was not willing to take the ark of the LORD into the city of David. But David took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
ESV.11: And the ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.
ESV.12: And it was told King David, “The LORD has blessed the household of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God.” So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom to the city of David with rejoicing.
ESV.13: And when those who bore the ark of the LORD had gone six steps, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened animal.
ESV.14: And David danced before the LORD with all his might. And David was wearing a linen ephod.
ESV.15: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and with the sound of the horn.
ESV.16: As the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out of the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart.
ESV.17: And they brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place, inside the tent that David had pitched for it. And David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
ESV.18: And when David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts
ESV.19: and distributed among all the people, the whole multitude of Israel, both men and women, a cake of bread, a portion of meat,  and a cake of raisins to each one. Then all the people departed, each to his house.
ESV.20: And David returned to bless his household. But Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, “How the king of Israel honored himself today, uncovering himself today before the eyes of his servants' female servants, as one of the vulgar fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!”
ESV.21: And David said to Michal, “It was before the LORD, who chose me above your father and above all his house, to appoint me as prince  over Israel, the people of the LORD — and I will celebrate before the LORD.
ESV.22: I will make myself yet more contemptible than this, and I will be abased in your  eyes. But by the female servants of whom you have spoken, by them I shall be held in honor.”
ESV.23: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

NASB.1: Now David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.
NASB.2: And David arose and went with all the people who were with him to Baale-judah, to bring up from there the ark of God which is called by the Name, the very name of the LORD of hosts who is enthroned [above] the cherubim.
NASB.3: They placed the ark of God on a new cart that they might bring it from the house of Abinadab which was on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were leading the new cart.
NASB.4: So they brought it with the ark of God from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill; and Ahio was walking ahead of the ark.
NASB.5: Meanwhile, David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all kinds of [instruments made of] fir wood, and with lyres, harps, tambourines, castanets and cymbals.
NASB.6: But when they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out toward the ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen nearly upset [it].
NASB.7: And the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down there for his irreverence; and he died there by the ark of God.
NASB.8: David became angry because of the LORD'S outburst against Uzzah, and that place is called Perez-uzzah to this day.
NASB.9: So David was afraid of the LORD that day; and he said, 'How can the ark of the LORD come to me?'
NASB.10: And David was unwilling to move the ark of the LORD into the city of David with him; but David took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
NASB.11: Thus the ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.
NASB.12: Now it was told King David, saying, 'The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, on account of the ark of God.' David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the city of David with gladness.
NASB.13: And so it was, that when the bearers of the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
NASB.14: And David was dancing before the LORD with all [his] might, and David was wearing a linen ephod.
NASB.15: So David and all the house of Israel were bringing up the ark of the LORD with shouting and the sound of the trumpet.
NASB.16: Then it happened [as] the ark of the LORD came into the city of David that Michal the daughter of Saul looked out of the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart.
NASB.17: So they brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent which David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
NASB.18: When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offering, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.
NASB.19: Further, he distributed to all the people, to all the multitude of Israel, both to men and women, a cake of bread and one of dates and one of raisins to each one. Then all the people departed each to his house.
NASB.20: But when David returned to bless his household, Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, 'How the king of Israel distinguished himself today! He uncovered himself today in the eyes of his servants' maids as one of the foolish ones shamelessly uncovers himself!'
NASB.21: So David said to Michal, '[It was] before the LORD, who chose me above your father and above all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel; therefore I will celebrate before the LORD.
NASB.22: 'I will be more lightly esteemed than this and will be humble in my own eyes, but with the maids of whom you have spoken, with them I will be distinguished.'
NASB.23: Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

CSB17.1: David again assembled all the fit young men in Israel: <sup>ⓝ</sup> thirty thousand.
CSB17.2: He and all his troops set out <sup>ⓐ</sup> to bring the ark of God from Baale-judah. <sup>[1]</sup> The ark bears the Name, the name of the LORD of Armies who is enthroned between the cherubim. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.3: They set the ark of God on a new cart and transported it from Abinadab’s house, which was on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, <sup>[2]</sup> sons of Abinadab, were guiding the cart <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.4: and brought it with the ark of God from Abinadab’s house on the hill. Ahio walked in front of the ark.
CSB17.5: David and the whole house of Israel were dancing before the LORD with all kinds of fir wood instruments, <sup>[3]</sup> lyres, harps, tambourines, sistrums, <sup>[4]</sup> and cymbals. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.6: When they came to Nacon’s threshing floor, Uzzah reached out to the ark of God and took hold of it because the oxen had stumbled.
CSB17.7: Then the LORD’s anger burned against Uzzah, <sup>ⓔ</sup> and God struck him dead on the spot for his irreverence, <sup>ⓕ</sup> and he died there next to the ark of God.
CSB17.8: David was angry because of the LORD’s outburst against Uzzah, so he named that place Outburst Against Uzzah, <sup>[5]</sup> as it is today.
CSB17.9: David feared the LORD that day and said, “How can the ark of the LORD ever come to me?”
CSB17.10: So he was not willing to bring the ark of the LORD to the city of David; <sup>ⓖ</sup> instead, he diverted it to the house of Obed-edom of Gath.
CSB17.11: The ark of the LORD remained in his house three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom <sup>ⓗ</sup> and his whole family.
CSB17.12: It was reported to King David: “The LORD has blessed Obed-edom’s family and all that belongs to him because of the ark of God.” So David went and had the ark of God brought up from Obed-edom’s house to the city of David with rejoicing. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.13: When those carrying the ark of the LORD advanced six steps, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.14: David was dancing <sup>[6]</sup> with all his might before the LORD wearing a linen ephod. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.15: He and the whole house of Israel were bringing up the ark of the LORD with shouts and the sound of the ram’s horn.
CSB17.16: As the ark of the LORD was entering the city of David, <sup>ⓛ</sup> Saul’s daughter Michal looked down from the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart.
CSB17.17: They brought the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent David had pitched for it. <sup>ⓜ</sup> Then David offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings in the LORD’s presence.
CSB17.18: When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the fellowship offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Armies.
CSB17.19: Then he distributed a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake to each one in the entire Israelite community, both men and women. <sup>ⓝ</sup> Then all the people went home.
CSB17.20: When David returned home to bless his household, <sup>ⓐ</sup> Saul’s daughter Michal came out to meet him. “How the king of Israel honored himself today!” she said. “He exposed himself today in the sight of the slave girls of his subjects like a vulgar person would expose himself.”
CSB17.21: David replied to Michal, “It was before the LORD who chose me over your father and his whole family to appoint me ruler over the LORD’s people Israel. <sup>ⓑ</sup> I will dance before the LORD,
CSB17.22: and I will dishonor myself and humble myself even more. <sup>[7]</sup> <sup>[8]</sup> However, by the slave girls you spoke about, I will be honored.”
CSB17.23: And Saul’s daughter Michal had no child to the day of her death.

WEB.1: David again gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.
WEB.2: David arose, and went with all the people who were with him, from Baale Judah, to bring up from there God’s ark, which is called by the Name, even the name of Yahweh of Armies who sits above the cherubim.
WEB.3: They set God’s ark on a new cart, and brought it out of Abinadab’s house that was on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new cart.
WEB.4: They brought it out of Abinadab’s house, which was in the hill, with God’s ark; and Ahio went before the ark.
WEB.5: David and all the house of Israel played before Yahweh with all kinds of instruments made of cypress wood, with harps, with stringed instruments, with tambourines, with castanets, and with cymbals.
WEB.6: When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached for God’s ark, and took hold of it; for the cattle stumbled.
WEB.7: Yahweh’s anger burned against Uzzah; and God struck him there for his error; and he died there by God’s ark.
WEB.8: David was displeased, because Yahweh had broken out against Uzzah; and he called that place Perez Uzzah,  to this day.
WEB.9: David was afraid of Yahweh that day; and he said, “How could Yahweh’s ark come to me?”
WEB.10: So David would not move Yahweh’s ark to be with him in David’s city; but David carried it aside into Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house.
WEB.11: Yahweh’s ark remained in Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house three months; and Yahweh blessed Obed-Edom and all his house.
WEB.12: King David was told, “Yahweh has blessed the house of Obed-Edom, and all that belongs to him, because of God’s ark.” So David went and brought up God’s ark from the house of Obed-Edom into David’s city with joy.
WEB.13: When those who bore Yahweh’s ark had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.
WEB.14: David danced before Yahweh with all his might; and David was clothed in a linen ephod.
WEB.15: So David and all the house of Israel brought up Yahweh’s ark with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.
WEB.16: As Yahweh’s ark came into David’s city, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out through the window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before Yahweh; and she despised him in her heart.
WEB.17: They brought in Yahweh’s ark, and set it in its place, in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before Yahweh.
WEB.18: When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Yahweh of Armies.
WEB.19: He gave to all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, both to men and women, to everyone a portion of bread, dates, and raisins. So all the people departed, each to his own house.
WEB.20: Then David returned to bless his household. Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, “How glorious the king of Israel was today, who uncovered himself today in the eyes of the servants of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!”
WEB.21: David said to Michal, “It was before Yahweh, who chose me above your father, and above all his house, to appoint me prince over the people of Yahweh, over Israel. Therefore I will celebrate before Yahweh.
WEB.22: I will be yet more vile than this, and will be base in my own sight. But of the servants of whom you have spoken, they will honor me.”
WEB.23: Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

NLT.1: Then David again gathered all the elite troops in Israel, 30,000 in all.
NLT.2: He led them to Baalah of Judah to bring back the Ark of God, which bears the name of the LORD of Heaven’s Armies, who is enthroned between the cherubim.
NLT.3: They placed the Ark of God on a new cart and brought it from Abinadab’s house, which was on a hill. Uzzah and Ahio, Abinadab’s sons, were guiding the cart
NLT.4: that carried the Ark of God. Ahio walked in front of the Ark.
NLT.5: David and all the people of Israel were celebrating before the LORD, singing songs and playing all kinds of musical instruments — lyres, harps, tambourines, castanets, and cymbals.
NLT.6: But when they arrived at the threshing floor of Nacon, the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out his hand and steadied the Ark of God.
NLT.7: Then the LORD’s anger was aroused against Uzzah, and God struck him dead because of this. So Uzzah died right there beside the Ark of God.
NLT.8: David was angry because the LORD’s anger had burst out against Uzzah. He named that place Perez-uzzah (which means “to burst out against Uzzah”), as it is still called today.
NLT.9: David was now afraid of the LORD, and he asked, “How can I ever bring the Ark of the LORD back into my care?”
NLT.10: So David decided not to move the Ark of the LORD into the City of David. Instead, he took it to the house of Obed-edom of Gath.
NLT.11: The Ark of the LORD remained there in Obed-edom’s house for three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and his entire household.
NLT.12: Then King David was told, “The LORD has blessed Obed-edom’s household and everything he has because of the Ark of God.” So David went there and brought the Ark of God from the house of Obed-edom to the City of David with a great celebration.
NLT.13: After the men who were carrying the Ark of the LORD had gone six steps, David sacrificed a bull and a fattened calf.
NLT.14: And David danced before the LORD with all his might, wearing a priestly garment.
NLT.15: So David and all the people of Israel brought up the Ark of the LORD with shouts of joy and the blowing of rams’ horns.
NLT.16: But as the Ark of the LORD entered the City of David, Michal, the daughter of Saul, looked down from her window. When she saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, she was filled with contempt for him.
NLT.17: They brought the Ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the special tent David had prepared for it. And David sacrificed burnt offerings and peace offerings to the LORD.
NLT.18: When he had finished his sacrifices, David blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Heaven’s Armies.
NLT.19: Then he gave to every Israelite man and woman in the crowd a loaf of bread, a cake of dates, and a cake of raisins. Then all the people returned to their homes.
NLT.20: When David returned home to bless his own family, Michal, the daughter of Saul, came out to meet him. She said in disgust, “How distinguished the king of Israel looked today, shamelessly exposing himself to the servant girls like any vulgar person might do!”
NLT.21: David retorted to Michal, “I was dancing before the LORD, who chose me above your father and all his family! He appointed me as the leader of Israel, the people of the LORD, so I celebrate before the LORD.
NLT.22: Yes, and I am willing to look even more foolish than this, even to be humiliated in my own eyes! But those servant girls you mentioned will indeed think I am distinguished!”
NLT.23: So Michal, the daughter of Saul, remained childless throughout her entire life.

AMP.1: Again David gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.
AMP.2: And David arose and went with all those who were with him to Baale-judah [Kiriath-jearim], to bring up from there [to Jerusalem] the ark of God which is called by the Name—the very Name of the LORD of hosts, who dwells enthroned above the cherubim.
AMP.3: They placed the ark of God on a new cart and brought it out of the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, sons of Abinadab, were leading the new cart.
AMP.4: So they brought it with the ark of God from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill; and Ahio was walking in front of the ark.
AMP.5: Meanwhile, David and all the house of Israel were celebrating and dancing before the LORD with all kinds of instruments made of fir or cypress wood, with lyres, harps, tambourines, castanets, and cymbals.
AMP.6: When they came to Nacon's threshing floor, Uzzah reached out [with his hand] to the ark of God and took hold of it, because the oxen [stumbled and] nearly overturned it.
AMP.7: And the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him there for his irreverence; and he died there by the ark of God.
AMP.8: David became angry and grieved and offended because of the Lord's outburst against Uzzah, and that place has been called Perez-uzzah (outburst against Uzzah) to this day.
AMP.9: So David was afraid of the LORD that day; and he said, "How can the ark of the LORD come to me?"
AMP.10: David was unwilling to move the ark of the LORD into the City of David with him; instead he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
AMP.11: So the ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household (family).
AMP.12: Now King David was told, "The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God." So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the City of David with rejoicing and gladness.
AMP.13: And when those who were carrying the ark of the LORD [by its poles] had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
AMP.14: And David was dancing before the LORD with great enthusiasm, and David was wearing a linen ephod [a priest's upper garment].
AMP.15: So David and all the house of Israel were bringing the ark of the LORD up [to the City of David] with shouts [of joy] and with the sound of the trumpet.
AMP.16: Then, as the ark of the LORD came into the City of David, Michal, Saul's daughter [David's wife], looked down from the window above and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she felt contempt for him in her heart [because she thought him undignified].
AMP.17: They brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent which David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
AMP.18: When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts (armies),
AMP.19: and distributed to all the people, the entire multitude of Israel, both to men and women, to each a [ring-shaped] loaf of bread, a cake of dates, and a cake of raisins. Then all the people departed, each to his house.
AMP.20: Then David returned to bless his household. But [his wife] Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, "How glorious and distinguished was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself and stripped [off his kingly robes] in the eyes of his servants' maids like one of the riffraff who shamelessly uncovers himself!"
AMP.21: So David said to Michal, "It was before the LORD [that I did this], who chose me above your father and all his house, to appoint me as ruler over Israel, the people of the LORD. Therefore I will celebrate [in pure enjoyment] before the LORD.
AMP.22: Yet I will demean myself even more than this, and will be humbled (abased) in my own sight [and yours, as I please], but by the maids whom you mentioned, by them I shall be held in honor."
AMP.23: Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

NET.1: David again assembled all the best men in Israel, thirty thousand in number.
NET.2: David and all the men who were with him traveled to Baalah in Judah to bring up from there the ark of God which is called by the name of the LORD of hosts, who sits enthroned between the cherubim that are on it.

NET.4: They brought it with the ark of God up from the house of Abinadab on the hill. Ahio was walking in front of the ark,
NET.5: while David and all Israel were energetically celebrating before the LORD, singing and playing various stringed instruments, tambourines, rattles, and cymbals.
NET.6: When they arrived at the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out and grabbed hold of the ark of God, because the oxen stumbled.
NET.7: The LORD was so furious with Uzzah, he killed him on the spot for his negligence. He died right there beside the ark of God.
NET.8: David was angry because the LORD attacked Uzzah; so he called that place Perez Uzzah, which remains its name to this very day.
NET.9: David was afraid of the LORD that day and said, “How will the ark of the LORD ever come to me?”
NET.10: So David was no longer willing to bring the ark of the LORD to be with him in the City of David. David left it in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.
NET.11: The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite for three months. The LORD blessed Obed-Edom and all his family.
NET.12: David was told, “The LORD has blessed the family of Obed-Edom and everything he owns because of the ark of God.” So David went and joyfully brought the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom to the City of David.
NET.13: Those who carried the ark of the LORD took six steps and then David sacrificed an ox and a fatling calf.
NET.14: Now David, wearing a linen ephod, was dancing with all his strength before the LORD.
NET.15: David and all Israel were bringing up the ark of the LORD, shouting and blowing trumpets.
NET.16: As the ark of the LORD entered the City of David, Saul’s daughter Michal looked out the window. When she saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, she despised him.
